newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan rupee ends firm in kerb, seen volatile.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan rupee ends firm in kerb, seen volatile.

text.p: The Pakistani rupee ended firm at 42 to the dollar in the kerb market on Thursday as uncertainty eased after the Supreme Court upheld President Farooq Leghari's November 5 dismissal of Benazir Bhutto's government, dealers said.
They said the rupee was likely to remain volatile next week amid nervousness before the February 3 national elections.
The State (central) Bank of Pakistan rate, last changed on October 22, was 40.1200/40.3206 rupees to the dollar.
The premium on foreign exchange bearer certificates ended at 5.0 percent compared to 4.75 percent in the morning.
